event: The United States conducted military strikes against targets in Iran on consecutive days, after which Iran launched attacks against U.S. military installations in Bahrain and Kuwait and against shipping vessels near the Strait of Hormuz.

framings.name: Nuclear Threat Elimination
framings.question: Did the United States successfully neutralize an existential nuclear threat before it was too late?
framings.key_claim: The U.S. strikes were a necessary and justified act of preemption to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, protecting American and allied security.
framings.description: This framing casts the strikes as a decisive, long-overdue response to Iran's advancing nuclear program. It foregrounds the danger of a nuclear-armed Iran and frames the military action as a success that degraded a generational threat.
framings.emphasizes: Iran's nuclear enrichment progress, the underground hardened facilities at Fordow and Natanz, the severity of damage inflicted, and the strategic logic of acting before Iran crossed the nuclear threshold.
framings.downplays: Uncertainty about actual damage to Iran's program, the diplomatic track that was underway, civilian casualties in Iran, and the broader regional escalation triggered by the strikes.
sample_headlines: Trump: Iran's Key Nuclear Enrichment Facilities Have Been 'Completely and Totally Obliterated'
Sen. Graham: Operation Midnight Hammer Was 'Necessary and Long Justified'

carriers.name: Donald Trump / White House
carriers.excerpt: Iran's key nuclear enrichment facilities have been completely and totally obliterated
carriers.role_evidence: Trump personally announced and framed the strikes as a total success against Iran's nuclear program in real-time Truth Social posts.

carriers.name: Sen. Lindsey Graham
carriers.excerpt: necessary and long justified
carriers.role_evidence: Graham publicly praised the strikes and predicted they could hasten the collapse of Iran's ruling regime, amplifying the preemption-success narrative.

carriers.name: Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA)
carriers.excerpt: Trump has been willing to do what's right and necessary to produce real peace in the region
carriers.role_evidence: Fetterman was the first Democratic senator to praise the strikes, providing bipartisan amplification of the nuclear-threat-elimination framing.

carriers.name: Senate Majority Leader John Thune
carriers.excerpt: commended Trump for confronting what he described as a persistent nuclear threat posed by Iran
carriers.role_evidence: As Senate Majority Leader, Thune's endorsement represents the Republican congressional leadership formally adopting this framing.

carriers.name: House Speaker Mike Johnson
carriers.excerpt: Iran declared war on us 47 years ago
carriers.role_evidence: Johnson defended Trump's decision to attack Iran on the House floor, framing it as a long-justified response to Iranian aggression.

carriers.name: Masih Alinejad (Iranian-American journalist/activist)
carriers.excerpt: was never about peaceful energy... built under a mountain to hide a nuclear program from the world
carriers.role_evidence: Alinejad's viral X post framed Fordow as proof of Iran's deceptive nuclear ambitions, amplifying the preemption narrative from a dissident perspective.

framings.name: Presidential War Powers / Constitutional Crisis
framings.question: Did the President have the legal authority to order these strikes without congressional authorization?
framings.key_claim: The strikes represent an unconstitutional usurpation of Congress's war-making power, setting a dangerous precedent for unchecked executive military action.
framings.description: This framing centers on the separation of powers and the War Powers Resolution of 1973. It asks whether the President acted lawfully by ordering sustained military operations without a congressional declaration of war or formal authorization.
framings.emphasizes: The absence of a congressional vote, the 60-day War Powers clock, bipartisan concern from lawmakers, and the pattern of Trump bypassing Congress on military action.
framings.downplays: The strategic rationale for the strikes, the nuclear threat posed by Iran, and the historical precedent of presidents acting unilaterally in military crises.
sample_headlines: After Iran Strikes, Congress Confronts Its Limited Power Over War
Trump's Iran Strikes Are Unconstitutional
House Passes War Powers Resolution Directing Trump to End Hostilities with Iran

carriers.name: Brennan Center for Justice
carriers.excerpt: The president acted unilaterally and lawlessly — without congressional authorization and absent any imminent threat
carriers.role_evidence: Published one of the earliest and most detailed legal arguments that the strikes were unconstitutional, framing the issue as executive overreach.

carriers.name: Sen. Tim Kaine (D-VA) & Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY)
carriers.excerpt: bipartisan measure... would require the president to obtain explicit congressional authorization before engaging in further hostilities
carriers.role_evidence: Kaine and Paul co-led the Senate war powers resolution, giving the constitutional framing bipartisan legislative legs.

carriers.name: Sen. Chuck Schumer
carriers.excerpt: urged Congress to reconvene quickly to reassert its constitutional role
carriers.role_evidence: As Senate Minority Leader, Schumer's public call to reconvene Congress drove mainstream media coverage of the war powers debate.

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
carriers.excerpt: a potentially illegal campaign that risks pulling the United States into a deeper Middle East conflict
carriers.role_evidence: PBS/AP framed the strikes as a constitutional referendum from day one, driving broad public awareness of the war powers debate.

carriers.name: NPR
carriers.excerpt: the clearest rebuke yet of President Trump's handling of the conflict
carriers.role_evidence: NPR's coverage of the House war powers vote framed it as a historic constitutional rebuke, amplifying the framing to a broad audience.

carriers.name: NBC News
carriers.excerpt: Trump says he doesn't need congressional authorization for Iran operations
carriers.role_evidence: NBC's reporting on Trump's letter to Congress and expert legal pushback kept the war powers framing alive through the ceasefire period.

carriers.name: Time Magazine
carriers.excerpt: they had been informed of the operation but given no role in approving it
carriers.role_evidence: Time's deep-dive on congressional impotence gave the war powers framing a major mainstream platform.

carriers.name: Donald Trump
carriers.excerpt: in a meaningless vote... limit my War Powers, right in the middle of my final negotiations
carriers.role_evidence: Trump's Truth Social post dismissing the House war powers vote as 'meaningless' and 'unpatriotic' represents the primary pushback against this framing.

framings.name: Escalation Spiral / Risk of Wider War
framings.question: Is this tit-for-tat exchange of strikes pulling the region—and the world—into an uncontrollable wider war?
framings.key_claim: The consecutive U.S. strikes and Iranian retaliations represent a dangerous escalation ladder with no clear off-ramp, risking a catastrophic regional or global conflict.
framings.description: This framing focuses on the dynamic of action and retaliation, asking whether either side has a strategy to de-escalate. It treats the strikes not as a discrete event but as a node in an accelerating cycle of violence.
framings.emphasizes: The consecutive nature of the strikes, Iran's retaliatory attacks on multiple countries, the risk of miscalculation, the spread of the conflict to Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, and shipping lanes.
framings.downplays: The strategic objectives of either side, the effectiveness of missile defense interceptions, and diplomatic back-channels.
sample_headlines: How Will Iran and the Middle East Respond to U.S. Strikes?
Iran Attacks Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan Again After New Waves of US Strikes
The Strikes Hold the Potential to Catalyze the Region Into One of Two Key Directions

carriers.name: CSIS / Mona Yacoubian
carriers.excerpt: either compelling Iran toward negotiations... or a widening conflict with regional and even global reverberations
carriers.role_evidence: CSIS published one of the first major analytical pieces framing the strikes as a binary fork between de-escalation and widening war.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: Iran has again claimed attacks on United States military bases in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's continuous live coverage of each new exchange of strikes drove global awareness of the escalation spiral framing.

carriers.name: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR)
carriers.excerpt: The attack quickly escalated into a regional war with widespread ramifications for critical supply chains and humanitarian aid
carriers.role_evidence: CFR's Global Conflict Tracker framed the event as a full regional war with cascading consequences, amplifying the escalation narrative to a policy audience.

carriers.name: Fareed Zakaria (CNN/Washington Post)
carriers.excerpt: the strikes undermined the rules-based international order
carriers.role_evidence: Zakaria argued the strikes would not prevent Iran from eventually getting nuclear weapons and would destabilize the international order, amplifying the escalation-risk framing.

carriers.name: Congressional Research Service (CRS)
carriers.excerpt: ongoing conflict, with ongoing U.S. and Israeli operations in Iran and Iranian retaliatory strikes on a range of targets
carriers.role_evidence: CRS's nonpartisan report to Congress formally documented the escalation spiral, giving it institutional weight in congressional deliberations.

framings.name: Global Economic Catastrophe / Energy Security
framings.question: What is the economic cost of this conflict to ordinary people worldwide, and who bears it?
framings.key_claim: Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for U.S. strikes has triggered the worst global energy supply disruption in history, threatening inflation, recession, and food insecurity worldwide.
framings.description: This framing shifts focus from military and political actors to the economic consequences felt by consumers, businesses, and vulnerable populations globally. It treats the Strait of Hormuz closure as the central event, not the strikes themselves.
framings.emphasizes: Oil price spikes, shipping disruptions, food insecurity, fuel shortages in Asia and the Global South, and the IEA's characterization of the crisis as historically unprecedented.
framings.downplays: The security rationale for the strikes, Iranian aggression, and the political dimensions of the conflict.
sample_headlines: Iran War: How High Could Oil Prices Get with Strait of Hormuz Closure?
What the Closure of the Strait of Hormuz Means for the Global Economy
Oil Prices Jump After Iran and U.S. Attack Commercial Ships

carriers.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
carriers.excerpt: the greatest global energy security challenge in history
carriers.role_evidence: The IEA's characterization of the crisis as historically unprecedented was the single most-cited framing device for the economic catastrophe narrative.

carriers.name: Bloomberg Economics
carriers.excerpt: a stagflationary shock that could shift everything from the path ahead for central banks to the outcome of the US midterm elections
carriers.role_evidence: Bloomberg's interactive oil-price scenario analysis went viral among financial and policy audiences, mass-amplifying the economic catastrophe framing.

carriers.name: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas
carriers.excerpt: a closure of the Strait of Hormuz... is expected to raise the average WTI price of oil to $98 per barrel and lower global real GDP growth by an annualized 2.9 percentage points
carriers.role_evidence: The Dallas Fed's quantitative modeling gave the economic catastrophe framing authoritative, data-driven credibility.

carriers.name: CNBC
carriers.excerpt: Oil prices are being whipsawed by developments in the Middle East once again
carriers.role_evidence: CNBC's real-time market coverage of oil price spikes tied each new military exchange directly to economic consequences for a mass financial audience.

carriers.name: World Food Programme (Carl Skau)
carriers.excerpt: 45 million more people would face acute hunger by July if the price of oil remained above $100 a barrel
carriers.role_evidence: WFP's acting director's CNN interview warning of acute hunger for millions reframed the economic story as a humanitarian crisis, dramatically broadening its reach.

carriers.name: Congressional Research Service (CRS)
carriers.excerpt: Congressional concern has risen in the wake of the February-March 2026 conflict as regional stability remains uncertain
carriers.role_evidence: CRS formally briefed Congress on Hormuz energy impacts, institutionalizing the economic framing in legislative deliberations.

framings.name: Human Cost / Civilian Harm
framings.question: Who is being killed, injured, and displaced—and are civilian lives being adequately protected?
framings.key_claim: The exchange of strikes has inflicted significant civilian harm in Iran, the Gulf states, and beyond, with Iranian attacks striking apartment buildings, airports, and desalination plants, while U.S.-Israeli strikes damaged schools and hospitals in Iran.
framings.description: This framing centers the human beings caught in the crossfire—Iranian civilians near nuclear sites, Gulf residents under Iranian missile barrages, and global populations facing food and water insecurity. It asks whether the laws of armed conflict are being respected.
framings.emphasizes: Civilian casualties in Iran and Gulf states, strikes on non-military infrastructure (desalination plants, airports, hotels, schools), displacement, and the humanitarian ripple effects of the Hormuz closure.
framings.downplays: Military objectives, the effectiveness of air defenses in limiting casualties, and the strategic context of the conflict.
sample_headlines: Iran's Retaliatory Strikes Challenge Image of Gulf Stability
Iran Continues Striking Civilian Infrastructure and US Bases in the Gulf
Ripple Effects from the Iran War Are Increasing the Risks of Acute Hunger for Millions

carriers.name: Time Magazine
carriers.excerpt: Five-star resorts in the glitzy tourist areas of Dubai, apartment buildings in Bahrain, and international airports have all been struck
carriers.role_evidence: Time's vivid on-the-ground reporting on civilian areas struck by Iranian missiles was among the first to foreground the human cost to Gulf residents.

carriers.name: FDD's Long War Journal
carriers.excerpt: targeting energy infrastructure, airports, military bases, government buildings, and urban areas
carriers.role_evidence: Long War Journal's granular daily tracking of Iranian strikes on civilian infrastructure provided the factual foundation for the civilian harm framing.

carriers.name: Iran's UN Ambassador
carriers.excerpt: more than 1,500 civilians have been killed so far, including at least 175 people who were killed by a reported U.S. strike on an Iranian elementary school
carriers.role_evidence: Iran's UN ambassador was among the first to formally assert civilian casualty figures and specific incidents of civilian harm, originating this framing in international forums.

carriers.name: World Food Programme / NBC News
carriers.excerpt: In many places, we're already taking from the hungry to give to the starving
carriers.role_evidence: WFP's CNN/NBC interviews on acute hunger linked the military strikes directly to mass civilian suffering globally, mass-amplifying the human cost framing.

carriers.name: Democratic Rep. Diana DeGette
carriers.excerpt: reckless actions are going to put the lives of American service members and American citizens at risk
carriers.role_evidence: DeGette was among the first elected officials to foreground risk to human life as the primary objection to the strikes.

framings.name: Diplomatic Failure / Negotiation Sabotage
framings.question: Did the strikes destroy a viable diplomatic path to a nuclear deal, and can negotiations be salvaged?
framings.key_claim: The U.S. strikes came while diplomatic negotiations were actively underway, collapsing a promising process and making a negotiated settlement far harder to achieve.
framings.description: This framing treats the strikes as a choice made against a live diplomatic alternative. It asks whether military force was truly necessary given that five rounds of indirect talks had already taken place, and whether the strikes have made Iran less or more likely to negotiate.
framings.emphasizes: The five rounds of U.S.-Iran indirect talks prior to the strikes, Iran's cancellation of a sixth round after the Israeli attack, the IAEA's withdrawal of inspectors, and the difficulty of resuming talks.
framings.downplays: Iran's nuclear progress during negotiations, the argument that military pressure creates negotiating leverage, and Iran's own bad-faith actions.
sample_headlines: Fareed Zakaria: The Only Way to Ensure Iran Does Not Obtain Nuclear Weapons Is Through Diplomacy
Iran: Impacts of June 2025 Israel and US Strikes — Outlook for Iran's Nuclear Programme
US Announces Return to Talks with Iran Over Its Nuclear Programme

carriers.name: Fareed Zakaria (CNN/Washington Post)
carriers.excerpt: the only way to ensure that Iran does not obtain nuclear weapons is through diplomacy
carriers.role_evidence: Zakaria was among the first prominent commentators to argue the strikes undermined the only reliable path to preventing Iranian nuclear weapons.

carriers.name: Congressional Research Service (CRS)
carriers.excerpt: Iran canceled a sixth round... Iran could also attempt to engage diplomatically with the United States
carriers.role_evidence: CRS's nonpartisan briefing documented the diplomatic timeline and Iran's cancellation of talks, providing the factual backbone for the diplomatic-failure framing.

carriers.name: House of Commons Library
carriers.excerpt: The US has announced a return to talks with Iran over its nuclear programme, though Iran says the US must first rule out any further military action
carriers.role_evidence: The UK Parliament's research arm documented the post-strike diplomatic impasse, amplifying the framing to an international policy audience.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: Progress towards a peace deal also remains slow... sticking points remain, with Iran demanding the release of frozen assets
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's ongoing coverage of stalled negotiations consistently framed the military exchanges as obstacles to a diplomatic resolution.

carriers.name: IAEA
carriers.excerpt: The IAEA has not been able to inspect the attacked Iranian nuclear facilities
carriers.role_evidence: The IAEA's withdrawal of inspectors and inability to verify damage formally institutionalized the argument that the strikes undermined the international verification regime.

framings.name: Effectiveness Doubt / Strategic Miscalculation
framings.question: Did the strikes actually achieve their stated military objective, or did they merely delay Iran's nuclear program while triggering catastrophic blowback?
framings.key_claim: Conflicting U.S. government assessments and a leaked DIA report suggest the strikes may have set back Iran's nuclear program by only months, not years, while triggering consequences—Hormuz closure, regional war—far worse than the threat they addressed.
framings.description: This framing questions the military and strategic logic of the operation on its own terms. It does not oppose the goal of preventing Iranian nuclear weapons but asks whether the chosen means were effective and whether the costs outweigh the benefits.
framings.emphasizes: The leaked DIA report suggesting Iran moved enriched uranium before the strikes, conflicting official assessments (months vs. years of setback), the Hormuz closure, and the reconstitution of Iran's nuclear program.
framings.downplays: The genuine damage inflicted on Iranian facilities, the argument that even a partial setback was worth achieving, and the deterrent signal sent to other proliferators.
sample_headlines: Leaked DIA Report: Strikes Set Back Iran's Nuclear Program by Only Months
Sen. Murkowski: 'It's a Year Later and We're Still Trying to Decide' If Iran's Nuclear Capabilities Were Truly Dismantled
IAEA Has Not Been Able to Inspect the Attacked Iranian Nuclear Facilities

carriers.name: U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (leaked report)
carriers.excerpt: the strikes set back Iran's nuclear program by months... the sites targeted were significantly damaged but not destroyed
carriers.role_evidence: The leaked DIA low-confidence assessment directly contradicted official Pentagon claims and originated the effectiveness-doubt framing.

carriers.name: Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK)
carriers.excerpt: It's a year later and we're still trying to decide that
carriers.role_evidence: Murkowski's skeptical comment to Time about whether the strikes truly dismantled Iran's nuclear capabilities gave the effectiveness-doubt framing rare Republican credibility.

carriers.name: IAEA
carriers.excerpt: The IAEA has not been able to inspect the attacked Iranian nuclear facilities
carriers.role_evidence: The IAEA's inability to verify damage provided an authoritative institutional basis for doubting official U.S. claims of success.

carriers.name: Congressional Research Service (CRS)
carriers.excerpt: U.S. government reports have provided differing assessments of the June strikes' impacts
carriers.role_evidence: CRS formally documented the contradictions between the 2025 National Security Strategy ('significantly degraded') and the 2026 National Defense Strategy ('obliterated'), institutionalizing the effectiveness-doubt framing.

carriers.name: Vox
carriers.excerpt: Israel's goal in the war may be regime change in Iran, rather than a simple targeting of their nuclear program
carriers.role_evidence: Vox questioned whether the stated nuclear-degradation objective was the real goal, amplifying doubts about the strategic coherence of the operation.

framings.name: Iranian Sovereignty / Aggressor Narrative
framings.question: Were the U.S. strikes an unprovoked act of aggression against a sovereign nation, and is Iran's retaliation legitimate self-defense?
framings.key_claim: The U.S. strikes constitute an illegal act of war against a sovereign state, and Iran's retaliatory attacks on U.S. military installations are a proportionate exercise of its right to self-defense under international law.
framings.description: This framing, prominent in Iranian state media, parts of the international left, and some international law circles, inverts the aggressor/defender roles. It treats the U.S. as the initiating belligerent and Iran's responses as legally and morally justified.
framings.emphasizes: Iran's sovereignty, the absence of a UN Security Council authorization for the strikes, Iran's framing of its responses as 'Operation True Promise,' and the targeting of U.S. military (not civilian) installations.
framings.downplays: Iran's nuclear program, its support for proxy forces, its crackdown on domestic protesters, and the civilian harm caused by Iranian missile barrages.
sample_headlines: IRGC: US Attacked 'Under False Pretenses,' Damaging Water Tanks and Telecommunications Towers
Iran Declares Strait of Hormuz 'Closed Until Further Notice' in Response to US 'Repeated Violations'
Iran Rejects Claims It Intended to Attack the US, Citing Aggressive US Military Posture

carriers.name: IRGC / Iranian State Media (IRIB, Tasnim, Fars)
carriers.excerpt: the war-mongering American regime attacked several points... under false pretenses
carriers.role_evidence: The IRGC's official statements, carried by state media, originated and consistently maintained the sovereignty/self-defense framing for Iranian domestic and international audiences.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: The IRGC warned that its forces remain fully prepared to deliver a 'crushing and decisive' response
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's coverage gave significant platform to IRGC statements and Iranian government framing, amplifying the sovereignty narrative to a global English-language audience.

carriers.name: Iran's UN Ambassador
carriers.excerpt: more than 1,500 civilians have been killed so far
carriers.role_evidence: Iran's UN ambassador formally presented the sovereignty/civilian harm framing in the UN Security Council, giving it institutional standing in international law forums.

carriers.name: House of Commons Library
carriers.excerpt: Iran says 'tensions could escalate irreversibly' if the snapback sanctions power is used
carriers.role_evidence: The UK Parliament's neutral research briefing documented Iran's sovereignty-based objections without endorsing them, giving them a mention in Western policy discourse.

carriers.name: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM)
carriers.excerpt: The strikes are in response to Iran's unwarranted and continued aggression
carriers.role_evidence: CENTCOM's official statements directly contested the Iranian sovereignty framing by characterizing U.S. strikes as responses to Iranian aggression, not unprovoked attacks.

gap_analysis: (framings-only — shared foundation, omissions, and gap analysis were skipped)

coverage_lean.event: The United States conducted military strikes against targets in Iran on consecutive days, after which Iran launched attacks against U.S. military installations
coverage_lean.skew: one-sided: no right-of-center coverage found (possible blindspot)
